text.p: These are some of the main stories in Sofia newspapers on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- Bulgarian citizens and firms have withdrawn some $743 million from their bank accounts in commercial banks for the first nine months of 1996, the central bank said. Hard currency deposits in commercial banks fell to $1.379 billion in the beginning of October, down from $2.122 billion at the end of December last year.
-- An International Monetary Fund mission is expected to arrive in Bulgaria on Wednesday to review implementation of the structural reform programme, the newspaper said without quoting sources.
-- The Czech Investment and Post Bank is expected to extend a $150-200 million credit to Bulgaria for the reconstruction of Sofia Airport, the airport's executive director Danyo Adanev said.

-- The European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) is interested in direct investment or granting of credits to the privatised structures of state-owned Bulgarian Telecommunication Company which plans to offer 25 percent of its capital to private investors, according the EBRD programme for Bulgaria.

-- The lev is expected to reach an exchange rate of 637 per dollar by the end of the year 2000, while cumulative inflation is expected to fall to 20 percent and the main interest rate to 12 percent, according to the government Agency for Economic Forecasts. At present the central bank's dollar fix is 216 levs per dollar, cumulative inflation is 153 percent and the key interest rate is set to a record high of 300 percent.
-- Bulgaria's voucher privatisation funds could merge with one another after the first mass privatisation tender under a regulation proposed by the Securities and Stock Exchanges Commission.
-- Four commercial banks have appealed to the country's Supreme Court against the central bank's decision of September 24 to put them under special supervision.

-- Petrol and diesel prices are expected to rise by some 10 percent and 22 percent respectively in the second increase this month under a proposal by the National Prices Committee which has yet to be approved by the cabinet.

-- Direct foreign investment to Bulgaria for the first nine months of 1996 totalled $201.109 million, which is 2.19 times more than the same period last year, deputy prime minister Roumen Gechev said.
-- A home-made bomb exploded in a car in Sofia at about 2 p.m. on Sunday, killing the owner of the car, 36 year old businessman Zhasmin Neichev, the interior ministry said.
